request.task: T0 corrected Canvas Agent Studio audit scope, authority cage, and baseline
request.head: 899b39433c4be242b4b3adcd39f3e6cd53df99c0

findings.scenario: T0 claims to freeze named Canvas contracts A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, G1–G9, and M1 from docs/specs/2026-08-16-canvas-upgrade.md as indexed by docs/plans/one-box-master/02-canvas/index.md. Those IDs are bound only by name plus the repo commit/tree; unlike Local Canvas and API surface they have no file or section SHA-256. An auditor cannot detect a later subsection swap or a wrong A/B/G/M byte range, so the named-criteria half of the required hash bind is missing.
findings.remediation: At tree 7a1a54e421d12cf7e5cc5a1f42877d8ffe6750b5 record SHA-256 for canvas-upgrade.md, the canvas index, and each named criterion’s exact inclusive/exclusive byte range (encoding and trailing-newline rule stated).

audit.proof_assessment: Byte counts that can be recomputed from embedded transcripts match the artifact (verify:plans stdout 247; focused vitest stdout 698). Exit 0, shared cwd, spawnSync argv, three transcriptSha256 fields, authority-packet SHA-256, and baselineEvidence:false for the zsh [id] glob are internally consistent. Tree/section/transcript SHA-256 values and OBX-AUTH-ATF-001 itself are not recomputable from this slice; they are claims, not checked oracles. Named Canvas criteria are not section-hashed. The path cage is not self-contained. The transcript preimage function is not uniquely specified.
residual_risks: Section, tree, authority-packet, and transcript SHA-256 values cannot be verified without re-reading the frozen tree or re-running the commands.
npm run still may invoke an inner script shell even when the outer spawnSync sets shell false.
test:plans is bound only by a 9183-byte hash plus an editorial tail, so the 48/48 oracle cannot be inspected from the receipt.
Focused 8-file/37-test baseline does not execute the three Canvas E2E harnesses listed in the inventory, so named A/B/G/M contracts are scoped on paper only.
Prohibited persistent-storage versus the retained persistent selection-scoped composer can still be misread as a write grant if the dependency disclaimer is ignored.
